lead: One price per reservation. No subscription, no account fee and no airfare to pay.
body: ## What the price covers

Each plan covers the preparation and delivery of one flight reservation document: your itinerary as a PDF with a booking reference, sent to your email. You pay for the document. The airfare is never part of the price, because you are not buying a seat on a flight.
> The prices shown on this page are placeholders until they are confirmed. The final price is always shown at checkout before you pay.
## Choosing the right plan

- **One-way** suits proof of onward travel. It is a single flight out of a country, often asked for by airlines and border officers. Read more on the [onward ticket page](/onward-ticket).
- **Return** gives an outbound and a return flight. It suits most visitor visa applications where the form asks for entry and exit dates. See the [return ticket page](/return-ticket).
- **Multi-city** covers several connected flights, for longer trips or itineraries with more than one stop.
If you are applying for a Schengen visa and visiting several countries, read the [Schengen visa guide](/dummy-ticket-for-schengen-visa) to see how the itinerary should line up with your form.
## What every plan includes

- A flight reservation with a booking reference (PNR)
- Your name as it appears on the passport
- Route, dates and flight details
- A PDF itinerary delivered by email
- Email support if a name or date needs correcting
## What you never pay for

You do not pay for an airline ticket, a seat, luggage or airline taxes. You also do not pay a subscription or create an account. If a payment method or extra charge applies, it is shown at checkout before you confirm.
## What affects the choice more than price

Price is rarely the main question. A better question is: **what does my embassy or airline ask for?** If the answer is a paid ticket, a reservation will not meet that requirement, and a refundable fare is the safer choice. Our guide to [airline hold and fare-lock options](/blog/airline-hold-booking-options) compares them.
## Refunds and changes

Refund terms are shown at checkout before you pay, so you can read them first. If a name or date on your itinerary is wrong, contact support with your order reference. The [refund policy](/refund-policy) page describes how requests are handled in general terms.
## Before you pay

1. Check the passport spelling of every name.
2. Confirm the dates against your application form.
3. Read the validity window and refund terms at checkout.
When you are ready, [see how it works](/how-it-works) or go straight to ordering.
## Pricing questions
## How to compare prices honestly

When you compare providers, check what exactly is included. Ask whether the price covers delivery by email, corrections to names and dates, and a refund route, and whether any extra fees appear at checkout. A low headline price that grows at the last step is not a low price. On this site the total is shown before you confirm the order.

Q: Is there a discount for several travellers?
A: Checkout shows the total for your trip before you pay. If a multi-traveller price applies, you will see it there.

Q: Are there any hidden fees?
A: The total price is shown at checkout before you confirm. You do not pay airline fares or taxes.

Q: Which plan do most visa applicants need?
A: It depends on what the application asks for. A return itinerary is common for visitor visas, and a one-way itinerary is common for proof of onward travel.
